newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Coffee still weak, may breach $1,500.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Coffee still weak, may breach $1,500.

text.p: NOV Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures are still looking vulnerable after last week's losses and technical analysts said on Monday the benchmark November could well breach the psychological $1,500 suppport.
Traders called the market to open $47 down on numbers but added in practice, it could do $20-$30 lower.
New York arabica coffee futures ended sharply lower on Friday as locals and speculators sold in anticipation of a build up in U.S. warehouse inventories during July.
After the market had closed, the Green Coffee Association (GCA) of New York's monthly data showed a 219,000-bag increase in stocks against most expectations of 50,000 to 150,000.
On the charts, the London November contract could take out the important $1,500 support, said Elli Gifford, an independent technical analyst.
The contract broke the previous key $1,600 support last week.
Next key support was pegged at $1,385.
Upside potential remained limited, although the initial goal was seen at just above $1,540. But Gifford said substantial resistance was at $1,640, the peak seen early last week.
Broker GNI said the GCA news could create a sell off in New York at the start of this week, particularly as the U.S. technicals were now following the London lead and turning negative.
"However London has been predominantly sold off on the back of the slump in the Indonesian rupiah as the currency has floated," it said in a commentary on Monday.

In other news, Vietnam's next coffee crop is expected to be a bumper one with yields of robusta and arabica reaching as much as 350,000 tonnes, according to the head of the Vietnam Coffee Corporation (Vinacafe).
Tran Khai was quoted by the English-language Vietnam News on Saturday as saying the 1997/98 crop would be Vietnam's biggest so far. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
